sections.vendors: No new supplier announcements from JLP this week; the latest partnership press release remains the 10 September interim results. Management said H1 saw 100+ new brands and products introduced and a new Sport and Wellness concept, while head-office restructuring (£35m exceptional costs) continues — so buying-team contacts may be shifting under the new structure.
sections.strategy: Will Kernan (ex-River Island CEO, JLP board member since 2023) is now in his first weeks as John Lewis MD after Peter Ruis exited on 6 September. JLP reiterated it will keep investing through the downturn, with ~£600m capex planned this year and a £50m John Lewis store programme covering Glasgow, Cambridge, Leicester, Reading and Liverpool; chair Jason Tarry has flagged that the full-year outcome now hinges on peak trading.
sections.pricing: Never Knowingly Undersold stays in place, and interim disclosures show John Lewis leaning on targeted promotions and clearance rather than broad price cuts — headline JL sales fell 2% to £2.0bn but full-price sales grew 5.5% thanks to tighter stock management. Own-brand AW26 knitwear is being positioned as accessible luxury, with cashmere crews at £99 (from £69) and pure merino at £45.
sections.launches: Press coverage this week (Woman & Home, 19 Sept) highlighted the AW26 own-brand edit: cashmere in 11 colourways, wool-rich pleated tailoring (£89), J. Lewis cotton trench (£329), organic cotton tees from £18, and chocolate/fig/moss as lead colours. The exclusive Amanda Wakeley range is now in its second season alongside partner brands 3.1 Phillip Lim, Topshop and Aligne.
sections.gossip: Market chatter continues around the widened H1 loss (LBTBE £89m vs £34m; £124m after exceptionals) and a cautious H2 outlook, with Bloomberg framing it as Britons reining in spending while costs rise. Kernan's arrival mid-reset makes the next few months a likely window for range and supplier reviews.
soWhat: Full-price sales up 5.5% while total JL sales fell shows JLP is buying tighter and clearing less — expect smaller initial orders, more in-season repeat buys and pressure on suppliers for shorter lead times and flexible MOQs.

Continued own-brand push into accessible natural fibres (cashmere, merino, wool-rich tailoring, organic cotton) keeps demand alive for premium cotton, RWS wool and GOTS-certified supply at sharp cost points — have certified, cost-engineered options ready for SS27/AW27 briefs.

A new MD plus head-office restructuring means buying relationships may be reshuffled; now is a good time to re-establish contact with category teams and position for range reviews before 2027 buying cycles lock in.
